A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DeCaFlow work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are readable and can be matched reliably, including relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic ablations, semi-synthetic Sachs and Ecoli70 experiments, and law-school fairness predictions in Section 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds a training-size experiment on the additive Sachs dataset in Appendix B.4.

M1.justification: The conditional-flow encoder and causal-flow decoder, posterior factorization, ELBO with warm-up regularization, and intervention/counterfactual algorithms are retained. The more explicit descriptions in v3 do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic proxy tasks, semi-synthetic Sachs and Ecoli70 settings, and law-school fairness task. The new training-size sweep retains existing Sachs coverage; graph misspecification and stochastic interventions are discussed without new evaluations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in matched experiments, including CNF, ANM, DCM, Deconfounder, the oracle, and the fairness baselines. The new training-size ablation reuses the existing oracle and unaware CNF.

E3.justification: New Appendix B.4 varies training sample size while holding test size fixed and evaluating interventions at the 25th and 75th percentiles. Existing benchmark splits and protocols remain unchanged; clarification of validation-based hyperparameter selection is additional documentation.

E4.justification: Appendix B.4 adds an analysis of data scarcity and sample efficiency for ATE and counterfactual estimation. The latent-dimension/proxy, encoder-selection, encoder-factorization, and unidentifiable-effect analyses already appear in v2.

E5.justification: New Figure B.4 reports 95% confidence intervals over 10 realizations. Existing five-run summaries, confidence intervals, and Mann–Whitney tests are retained; the ten-realization design applies specifically to the added experiment.

E6.justification: Figure B.4 adds learning curves showing generally decreasing DeCaFlow and oracle errors as training data increase, while unaware CNF plateaus at higher errors. Matched numerical entries in Table 1 and v2 Tables 2–8 versus v3 Tables B.1–B.7 are unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal assumptions, definitions, propositions, corollaries, and Appendix A proofs are retained. Added discussion interprets existing assumptions, and the new Monte Carlo averaging expression in Appendix D explains the existing ATE estimator.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contribution claims retain their scope: one training process per dataset, causal estimation under hidden confounding, proxy/do-calculus identifiability, counterfactual guarantees under the stated assumptions, and favorable empirical comparisons.

C2.justification: v3 adds consequences of graph misspecification and explains the soft-versus-hard intervention mismatch for Sachs data. It interprets the new sample-size results, qualifies the explanation of Deconfounder’s counterfactual errors as a hypothesis, and removes F.1’s proposed indirect validation through another query sharing a confounder.

D1.justification: v2 promises code upon acceptance; v3 provides an implementation link, identifies a GPL license, and offers the full training/tuning/validation pipeline on request in the checklist. It also explicitly specifies a standard Gaussian latent prior and clarifies validation-MMD hyperparameter selection.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Knothe, Rosenblatt, Gretton et al., Oates et al., and Correa and Bareinboim, while removing the two Chen et al. references and D’Haultfoeuille. Appendix E.2 refines the NCM comparison and restricts its exogenous-identifiability positioning to unconfounded variables.

P1.justification: Copyediting and targeted rewrites clarify assumptions, proxy intuition, practical ablations, fairness, and related work. v3 adds a NeurIPS checklist and updates affiliations and the conference header, while retaining the main section order and appendix framework.

P2.justification: v3 adds the two-panel training-size Figure B.4, uses section-based appendix figure/table numbering, revises captions, and relocates retained displays, including the fairness table and timing tables. Existing plots and the overall visual format are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The added training-size study, clearer graph/intervention limitations, narrower validation advice in F.1, and concrete code-access information improve practical assessment and transparency. These are limited gains because the core proofs and benchmark results remain unchanged. The new finite-sample curves also do not establish B.4’s stronger assertion of vanishing estimation errors.
